extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry/number theory (readers familiar with Mochizuki's IUT framework and arithmetic of elliptic curves)
extracted.subtask_description: Constructing/identifying elliptic curves over arithmeticoids equipped with Initial Theta Data, defining Tate idele/divisor invariants, and proving explicit bounds (discriminant/conductor/prime bounds) used in proofs related to Mochizuki's results. Includes existence theorems, height comparisons, and ramification/discriminant estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bounding domain / compactly bounded subset
rubrics_metrics.description: A bounding domain in X_S is a G_S-stable, compact subset Z = \prod_{v\in S} Z_v such that Z is the closure of its interior; the finite set S is called the support. The S-supported compactly bounded subset Z(Z,S) of X(\overline{Q}) consists of points x \in X(\overline{Q}) such that for some finite extension M/L and every embedding ι: M \hookrightarrow \overline{Q}_v (v\in S) the image ι(x) lies in Z_v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to define the domain of arithmetic points under consideration. Example: for X = P^1 \setminus {0,1,\infty} one may take disjoint Galois-invariant compact annuli in archimedean and p-adic factors to form Z. The bounding domain (Z,S) uniquely determines the compactly bounded subset Z(Z,S). This notion is the basis for height- and finiteness-arguments that follow (e.g., in Theorem 5.7.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tate idele and Tate divisor (Idelic Tate divisors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an elliptic curve C/L and for each non-archimedean place v a choice q_v of a Tate parameter, the idele TI_{C/arith(L)} = (q_v)_{v\in V_{non,L}} \in \prod_{v\in V_L} L_v^* defines an arithmetic divisor Divisor(TI_{C/arith(L)}) = \sum_{v\in V_{non,L}} ord_v(q_v)\cdot v which is the Tate divisor q_{C/arith(L)}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different choices of local Tate parameters give the same Tate divisor; the idele viewpoint is convenient for passage to Galois cohomology (via Kummer theory L_v^*_{\widehat{\ } } \simeq H^1(G_{L_v},Q_p(1))). The tuple of theta-values gives a related divisor; one studies degrees and cohomology-classes arising from these ideles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 4.5.11 (collating Tate idele cohomology classes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a collection A of arithmeticoids/holomorphoids C/arith(L)_z and choices of Tate idele cohomology classes TI_{C/arith(L)_z} for each z in A, there exists a subset Ψ_{C,A} contained in H^1(arith(L)_{y0},Q(1)) (for a fixed standard arithmeticoid y0) that is the union, over z in A and over isomorphisms of factors, of the images of certain subsets Ψ_z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This proposition allows one to collate compatible systems of idele cohomology classes arising from many distinct arithmeticoids into a single Galois cohomology space; it is preparatory for volume and averaging arguments. The statement is constructive in terms of chosen TI classes and standard arithmeticoid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 4.5.12 (normalized arithmetic degree varies with arithmeticoid)
rubrics_metrics.description: For C/L and a collection A of arithmeticoids, choosing for each z in A a Tate idele TI_{C/arith(L)_z} (normalized for the standard arithmeticoid), the normalized arithmetic degree log(TI_{C/arith(L)_z}) is a function of z. In particular, for A = Y_L (the full set of holomorphoids) this yields a non-constant function 'normalized degree of the Tate divisor' Y_L \to R given by z \mapsto log(TI_{C/arith(L)_z}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes dependence of the normalized degree on the choice of arithmetic holomorphic structure, a fundamental observation used in averaging/volume heuristics. It motivates considering families of arithmeticoids rather than a single one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remarks on volumes and averaging over arithmeticoids (Remark 4.5.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Several observations: (1) interest in volume of Ψ_{C,A} inside H^1(arith(L)_{y0},Q(1)) for a suitable measure; (2) difficulty in concretely describing images of specific elements of Ψ_{C,A}; (3) practical computations use Bloch–Kato subspace H^1_e and an adelic tensor-product log-shell (Mochizuki's I_Θ) to compute volumes; (4)-(5) idealized integrals/averages over Y_L and product spaces Y_L^{\ell^*} are currently not directly available but guide heuristics; (6)-(7) analogies with Teichmüller theory and Mochizuki's log-volume computations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are methodological constraints and heuristics: one should work in cohomology and Bloch–Kato subspaces for explicit volume computations, and treat idealized integrals as motivating constructs rather than directly computable objects at present.

rubrics_metrics.name: The log-Different + log-Conductor Theorem (Theorem 4.6.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let C/L be an elliptic curve and M a finite extension of L. With notations f_L,f_M and d_L,d_M as defined, (1) (log d_M + log f_M) - (log d_L + log f_L) = (1/[M:Q]) \sum_{v\in V_{non,L}} \sum_{w|v} τ_{w|v}\, f_{w|v}\, log v where τ_{w|v}=0 iff w|v is tamely ramified; (2) the left-hand side is non-negative and each τ_{w|v} satisfies 0 \le τ_{w|v} \le ord_v(e_{w|v}); (3) the difference depends only on primes v of L which are wildly ramified in M/L; (4) equality holds (difference zero) iff M/L is tamely ramified; (5) if S_wild is set of rational primes below wildly ramified primes then (log d_M + log f_M) - (log d_L + log f_L) \le (#S_Q_wild)\, log[M:L].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the central arithmetic identity used to compare normalized arithmetic degrees/conductors/discriminants under field extensions. Use the formula (1) to bound changes coming only from wild ramification; consequences include non-negativity and explicit bounding by number/size of wild primes. The theorem is applied repeatedly to control discriminant/conductor growth in later bounds (e.g., Lemmas 6.4.1, 6.4.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 4.6.15 (uniform bound for families unramified outside S and tame outside Swild)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a family \mathcal{F}_L = \{M/L\} of finite extensions with [M:L] bounded, each M unramified outside a fixed finite set S and tamely ramified outside a fixed finite Swild, there exists c>0 depending on C,[M:L],Swild such that (log d_M + log f_M) - (log d_L + log f_L) \le c for all M in the family.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This corollary provides a uniform absolute bound on the discriminant+conductor difference across a family with controlled ramification; used to deduce boundedness of relevant arithmetic invariants in parameter families and in existence/compactness arguments for Initial Theta Data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 5.4.1 (Tate(C/M) and Tate_Ψ variants)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an elliptic curve C/M with Tate parameters q_w at non-archimedean places w, define Tate(C/M) = (1/[M:Q]) \sum_{w\in V_{non,M}} ord_w(q_w) \log w. For a finite set Ψ of rational primes define Tate_Ψ(C/M) = (1/[M:Q]) \deg(\sum_{w\nmid p \in Ψ} ord_w(q_w)\cdot w) (logarithmic degree of the portion not supported over Ψ). In particular Tate_{\{2\}} is denoted Tate2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These functions assign normalized logarithmic degrees of the Tate divisor (or portions thereof) and are used as height-like invariants for elliptic curves viewed over their field of moduli. Tate2 is important in applications (Mochizuki uses Ψ={2}).

rubrics_metrics.name: Height comparison (Proposition 5.6.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under hypotheses (bounded bounding-domain Z, condition (5.6.2)), one has equality of bounded discrepancy classes of functions on the compactly bounded set: (1/6)·Tate ≈ (1/6)·Tate2 ≈ h_\infty ≈ h_{\omega_{P^1}(D)} where h_\infty is pullback of the divisor at infinity on the moduli and h_{\omega_{P^1}(D)} is the natural logarithmic height on U.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This relates the Tate-invariants to classical height functions up to bounded discrepancies on the compactly bounded domain; it is used to connect arithmetic invariants (Tate) to heights and thereby invoke finiteness/height-bounds results (e.g., Silverman's theorem) in the existence proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of Initial Theta Data (Theorem 5.7.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given the setting (S-supported bounding domain Z, condition (5.6.2), bounds on degree), there exist finite exceptional sets Exc(Z,d) and constants (N, δ, d_mod, etc.) such that for any x_\lambda \in U(\overline{Q})^{\le d} \setminus Exc with corresponding Legendre curve C_\lambda and minimal field of definition L_mod, letting L = L_mod(\sqrt[5]{3\cdot 5}) and L_{tpd} = L_mod(C_\lambda[2]), there exists a prime ℓ satisfying explicit bounds (ℓ between Q^{1/2}/(10δ·log(2δ·log Q)) and Q^{1/2}·log(2δ·log Q)) for which C_\lambda satisfies Initial-Theta Data (as in Joshi [2024c] and Mochizuki).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the central existence theorem: outside a finite exceptional set of moduli points, one can choose a prime ℓ in an explicit numeric range so that the elliptic curve acquires the algebraic/Galois properties required for Initial Theta Data (control of torsion fields, multiplicative reduction primes, Galois representation fullness, etc.). The theorem is proved by combining height comparisons, prime-counting estimates, local/global ramification control, and auxiliary lemmas (5.8.x).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prime-selection lemmas (Lemmas 5.8.1, 5.8.2, 5.8.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical lemmas giving: (5.8.1) lower bounds on partial prime-sum θ(Q) and existence of primes in ranges relative to Q^{1/2}; (5.8.2) control of a finite set A of primes dividing certain local invariants av or equal to residue characteristics pv and bounding θ_A; (5.8.7) existence of a rational prime ℓ in a specified interval depending on Q and δ with properties: ℓ \nmid a_v for all v and if ℓ = p_v then a_v < Q^{1/2}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These lemmas provide the combinatorial/analytic number theory input needed to pick an admissible ℓ with required arithmetic properties; they rely on standard prime distribution estimates (e.g., Chebyshev/Dusart-type bounds).

rubrics_metrics.name: Finiteness and bounded-height lemmas (Lemmas 5.8.8 and 5.8.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma 5.8.8: For the chosen ℓ (as in 5.8.7) there are only finitely many elliptic curves in the bounded domain having an L-rational subgroup of order ℓ. Lemma 5.8.9: If an elliptic curve C_\lambda in the bounded set has all primes of multiplicative reduction lying in a prescribed (small) set, then C_\lambda has bounded height.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to enlarge the exceptional set Exc to discard problematic curves; together with height-finiteness results these give finiteness of exceptions and allow choosing curves with desired multiplicative reduction primes and Galois properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Galois representation fullness (Lemma 5.8.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the hypotheses and after excluding Exc, for C_\lambda the Galois representation on ℓ-torsion ρ_ℓ: G_L \to GL_2(F_ℓ) satisfies ρ_ℓ(G_L) \supset SL_2(F_ℓ) (in particular often has full GL_2 image).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This property is crucial for establishing the algebraic constraints in Initial Theta Data (control of mod-ℓ Galois image); it follows from standard results when multiplicative reduction and other local conditions are present and ℓ is chosen as in the prime-selection lemmas.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Main Bound (Theorem 6.1.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the assumptions (C with Initial Theta Data and notation of §5), for q = q_{C/L} the Tate divisor, one has inequalities of the form (1/6)·log(q) bounded above and below by expressions involving log(d_{L_{tpd}})+log(f_{L_{tpd}}), log(d_L)+log(f_L), d_{mod}, ℓ, and explicit constants: in particular (1/6)·log(q) \le (1+20/(d_{mod}·ℓ))·(log(d_{L_{tpd}})+log(f_{L_{tpd}})+20(e^*_{mod}·ℓ+60)) and a corresponding lower bound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the principal quantitative inequality relating the normalized Tate-degree to discriminant/conductor quantities and the auxiliary prime ℓ; it synthesizes the previous discriminant bounds, ramification divisors, and arithmetic inputs. The explicit constants (e.g., η_prm=60) and factors are given; the inequality is a reorganized version of Mochizuki's Theorem 1.10 and is used later to derive the main arithmetic consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prime counting explicit estimate (Proposition 6.2.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For x \ge η_prm := 60, the prime-counting function satisfies π(x) \le (4/3)·x/log x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explicit estimate (from Dusart-type bounds) is used repeatedly in counting/averaging arguments and in controlling contributions from primes in ramification divisors and s_{} constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global discriminant and conductor bounds (Lemmas 6.4.1 and 6.4.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inequalities comparing log(d_L)+log(f_L) and variants with those of L_{tpd} and L': (Lemma 6.4.1) log(d_L)+log(f_L) \le log(d_{L_{tpd}})+log(f_{L_{tpd}}) + 33/21 (an explicit additive bound computed from wild ramification contributions); (Lemma 6.4.2) for L' one has log(d_{L'})+log(f_{L'}) \le 4(log(d_{L_{tpd}})+log(f_{L_{tpd}})) + 2 log ℓ + 33/21, and corresponding multiplicative forms used in later bounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These bounds are consequences of the log-different+log-conductor theorem plus explicit counting of wild primes and degree bounds; they are key to replacing discriminant/conductor terms of larger fields by those of the 2-torsion extension L_{tpd} plus controlled error terms involving ℓ and small constants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ramification divisors and their normalized degrees (definitions (6.7.2)–(6.7.7) and Lemma 6.7.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define V^{dst}_{L^*} as the subset of primes of L^* ramiﬁed over Q (equivalently dividing 30·ℓ or appearing in supports of q_{L^*}+d_{L^*}). For L^* define s_{L^*} = \sum_{v\in V^{dst}_{L^*}} e_v\cdot v, its degree deg(s_{L^*}) = \sum_v e_v, and normalized degree log(s_{L^*}) = deg(s_{L^*})/[L^*:Q]. Also define s^{\le}_{L^*} with local weights ι_v = e^*_{mod} if p_v \le ℓ else 0. Lemma 6.7.8: e^*_{mod}·log(s^{\le})/(4/3) \le (e^*_{mod}·ℓ + η_{prm}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These constructions quantify ramification contributions coming from 'destination' primes (those that ramify in the auxiliary extension) and produce explicit numeric bounds used to control error terms in the main inequalities. The lemma gives a simple upper bound on normalized degree contributions supported at small primes up to ℓ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 6.8.1 (combined discriminant/ramification inequality)
rubrics_metrics.description: An explicit inequality combining d_{L'}, s_Q and d_{mod}, ℓ constants: 1 + (log(d_{L'}) + log(s_Q))/(4/ℓ)·(1+1/(12·d_{mod}/ℓ)) \le (4/ℓ)·(1 + ... ) with explicit constants (the displayed fragment in the text relates log(d_{L_{tpd}})+log(f_{L_{tpd}}), log ℓ and additive constants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This proposition is a technical step that bounds combined discriminant and ramification contributions in terms of smaller-field invariants and ℓ-dependent error terms; it feeds into the proof of the First Main Bound and is obtained by local counting of residue-field sizes and the log-different+log-conductor machinery.
